speaker: Doctor
text:
I'm Dr. Agent. I see you're pregnant and experiencing vaginal bleeding with abdominal pain; how many weeks along are you, and have you noticed any cramping or contractions?

REQUEST TEST: Complete blood count (CBC) and beta-hCG levels.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hemoglobin: 10.2 g/dL (decreased); Platelets: 200,000 /μL; PT: 11 seconds; aPTT: 30 seconds. Note: Ultrasound findings suggestive of uterine scar disruption and hemoperitoneum were also identified during the examination.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound findings of uterine scar disruption and hemoperitoneum are highly concerning for a uterine rupture; can you tell me if you have a history of a prior cesarean section or uterine surgery? Please stay here while we prepare for emergency intervention.

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1, at 38 weeks' gestation. The patient reports experiencing vaginal bleeding for the past hour accompanied by severe abdominal pain. She mentions that she felt contractions before the onset of the bleeding, but the contractions ceased once the bleeding began. Her first childbirth was a cesarean section due to nonreassuring fetal heart rate.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Uterine Rupture. REQUEST IMAGES: Immediate abdominal ultrasound and CT scan to confirm hemoperitoneum and assess fetal status. This is a life-threatening emergency; we must prepare for immediate Cesarean section and surgical repair.
